Description Are you passionate about translating scientific research into real-world impact at massive scale? PXT Central Science (PXTCS) builds the analytical foundations that shape how Amazon attracts, develops, and retains talent at a scale no other company operates. Our models and research directly influence decisions affecting over a million employees worldwide, from compensation and attrition strategy to employee engagement and workforce planning The L5 Research Scientist in Survey Science contributes to the science behind Amazon's state-of-the-art employee surveys, setting the standard for how Amazon measures what its employees are experiencing. The questions that matter most in this role are the ones numbers alone cannot settle, and that often run ahead of demand — identifying the challenges leaders will face before they ask, and building the methods to address them. How is the culture changing as the company evolves? What are employees experiencing that no metric on a dashboard captures? Where are employee concerns emerging that have not yet shown up in any data? These factors drive business outcomes, resist clean quantification, and require creative measurement approaches to address. Key job responsibilities - Design, develop, and evaluate mathematical, statistical, and machine learning models to address complex business problems, ensuring solutions are scalable, reliable, and performant in production environments. - Apply a breadth of scientific techniques — including generative AI approaches where appropriate — to frame ambiguous business challenges into well-defined research problems, working backwards from customer needs to identify the right methodology. - Collaborate with software development engineers and cross-functional partners to translate research prototypes into engineering specifications and production-ready systems, balancing scientific rigor with practical constraints. - Provide guidance on survey methods to teams across PXT, so employee research across Amazon meets a consistent standard. - Develop and audit metrics to quantify solution impact, measure project progress, and gate rollouts based on quality, while identifying opportunities for continuous model improvement. - Mentor other scientists and contribute to the broader scientific community through peer reviews, publications at internal or external venues, and active participation in hiring and team planning. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing experimental results from a model you deployed last week, then shift into a design discussion with engineering partners about integrating a new approach into an existing system. After lunch, you could be deep in data analysis, exploring patterns that inform your next hypothesis. You'll regularly present findings to teammates, provide scientific reviews for peers across the organization, and carve out time to stay current with the latest research in your field. About the team PXT Central Science is Amazon's people-science R&D organization. We develop causal inference methods, predictive models, and decision-support tools that operate at the intersection of economics, machine learning, and organizational science. Our work spans employee experience, workforce planning, compensation, talent acquisition, and employee relations — always grounded in rigorous methodology and always aimed at real-world impact. Your Team Responsibilities

The Factors Research Platform and Governance team is responsible for building and modernizing the infrastructure, tooling, and frameworks that power MSCI's quantitative risk and factor model research. The team develops the systems and environments that enable researchers to iterate quickly, maintain model governance, and deliver production-quality outputs at scale.

Your Key Ressponsibilities

  • Designing and building modern research infrastructure that integrates AI to accelerate model development, validation, and reporting workflows
  • Developing tools and frameworks that allow researchers to move from high-level specifications to production-ready implementations with minimal manual overhead
  • Building and maintaining automated validation, testing, and governance pipelines for quantitative models
  • Writing production-level code to support platform development and model delivery
  • Supporting existing factor and risk models while evolving the platform to enable faster research iteration
  • Collaborating cross-functionally with research, engineering, and data teams
  • Presenting complex systems and methods to a broad range of audiences

Your skills and experience that will help you excel

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Finance, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or other quantitative discipline
  • Strong software engineering skills, particularly in Python
  • Hands-on experience with modern AI-assisted development tools and workflows, with a demonstrated ability to stay current with rapidly evolving AI capabilities and incorporate them into day-to-day work
  • Experience building systems and tooling that leverage AI/LLMs to augment technical workflows
  • Data analysis and experience with large-scale data infrastructure
  • Econometrics and applied statistics
  • Ability to work independently and drive projects from design through delivery
  • Knowledge of finance or risk modeling is preferred but not required

About MSCI

What we offer you

  • Salary range: $201,000 - $261,000 / year. Plus eligible for annual bonus.
  • Transparent compensation schemes and comprehensive employee benefits, tailored to your location, ensuring your financial security, health, and overall wellbeing.
  • Flexible working arrangements, advanced technology, and collaborative workspaces.
  • A culture of high performance and innovation where we experiment with new ideas and take responsibility for achieving results.
  • A global network of talented colleagues, who inspire, support, and share their expertise to innovate and deliver for our clients.
  • Global Orientation program to kickstart your journey, followed by access to our Learning@MSCI platform, AI Learning Center, LinkedIn Learning Pro and tailored learning opportunities for ongoing skills development.
  • Multi-directional career paths that offer professional growth and development through new challenges, internal mobility and expanded roles.
  • We actively nurture an environment that builds a sense of inclusion belonging and connection, including eight Employee Resource Groups. All Abilities, Asian Support Network, Black Leadership Network, Climate Action Network, Hola! MSCI, Pride & Allies, Women in Tech, and Women’s Leadership Forum.

At MSCI we are passionate about what we do, and we are inspired by our vision – to power better decisions. You’ll be part of an industry-leading network of creative, curious, and entrepreneurial pioneers. Description Are you passionate about using data and machine learning to improve how Amazon reaches customers? The Customer Targeting team is looking for an Applied Scientist to build the science behind the targeting of Amazon's marketing initiatives across channels and ad formats. You will turn business questions into modeling problems and take your solutions from prototype to production, working closely with senior scientists, engineers, and business partners. We are moving targeting toward outcome-based optimization and an AI-native, agentic way of working. In this role you will work on online optimization and reinforcement learning, incrementality modeling, and the next generation of our segment-based targeting model. You will also help build agentic workflows that make targeting decisions transparent and bring science recommendations to the people using them. The right candidate has strong quantitative and statistical skills, hands-on experience with modern ML methods, and is comfortable working through ambiguity in a fast-paced environment. You pay close attention to detail, learn quickly, and work well in a highly collaborative team. Key job responsibilities - Build online optimization (e.g., TSO, bandits) and reinforcement learning methods that optimize targeting decisions for business outcomes rather than proxy metrics. - Develop incrementality and uplift models that estimate the causal impact of targeting, and use them to improve who we target and how much we spend. - Improve the existing segment-based targeting model: engineer and evaluate new features, migrate it to new model architectures, and build automated feedback loops that retrain and improve the model from observed outcomes. - Contribute to the intelligence layer of our agentic system: build components that explain targeting decisions and propose science-driven solutions to business partners. - Design and analyze experiments (A/B tests, causal inference methods) to measure the incremental impact of targeting changes. - Write production-quality model code and partner with engineers to deploy, monitor, and maintain models. - Present methods and results clearly, backed by data, with actionable recommendations for science and business stakeholders. About the team Predictive Targeting builds the systems that decide who sees Amazon's marketing content, and how often, across Amazon's stores and channels. We are engineers and scientists working on one shared problem: making sure customers see the most relevant and engaging marketing, and making each campaign better than the last. Description Applied Scientists on the AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) Builder Enablement team use program analysis, machine learning and generative AI for managing vulnerabilities and securing the software supply chain across AWS. Our scope covers the third-party open-source packages, language ecosystems, operating systems and kernels that AWS services are built on. Our goal is to take builders out of the remediation loop. When a vulnerability is disclosed or a package is compromised, our systems work out whether it actually affects AWS, generate the fix, check that it's safe and ship it at AWS scale, with one click or no clicks at all. New vulnerabilities are disclosed every day in the software AWS depends on, and finding and fixing them by hand doesn't scale. We build systems that detect vulnerabilities and work out whether the vulnerable code can actually be reached and exploited in a given service. They rank issues by real risk rather than raw severity scores, then fix them automatically. That can mean upgrading dependencies across ecosystems like Java, Python, JavaScript, Go and Rust, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches, or patching operating systems and kernels across the fleet. Just as important, we check that each fix is correct and safe, so it can merge with little or no human review. Beyond known vulnerabilities, we protect the integrity of the software supply chain itself. Modern software is assembled more than it is written, and every dependency is a potential way in for attackers. Securing it means knowing what's in our software, where it came from and whether it can be trusted. Our work here includes building and analyzing software bills of materials (SBOMs), verifying package provenance and build integrity, and detecting malicious or compromised packages before they reach production. Our methods range from static and dynamic program analysis to LLM-based agents for code repair and upgrades. This is a chance to shape a fast-growing area that directly affects the security of AWS and its customers. You'll apply your technical depth in a fast-moving environment, and your work will reach thousands of AWS builders and services. This includes vulnerability detection, reachability and exploitability analysis, dependency resolution, and prioritizing risk across third-party packages, operating systems and kernels. • Build program analysis techniques (static analysis, dataflow and call-graph analysis, binary and source analysis) that tell us precisely whether a vulnerability affects a given service or host. • Apply generative AI and agentic coding methods to fix vulnerabilities automatically. Examples include upgrading dependencies, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches and migrating code across language versions. • Develop ways to check that automated fixes are correct and safe, such as test generation, behavior-equivalence checking, build and runtime checks, and confidence scoring, so changes can merge with little or no human review. • Own the design, experiments and delivery of well-defined science problems from start to finish. Description Amazon Ads runs one of the largest real-time decision systems in the world. To meet advertiser goals, we process >4 million ad requests per second, and this team decides which of them are worth the compute. We mine a petabyte-scale stream of traffic to tell in-demand, valuable requests apart from wasteful ones, filtering out the noise and forwarding only what brings value to advertisers, all within milli-seconds. Our solutions save millions in compute costs and drive long-term growth for Amazon's Retail and Marketplace businesses. Why you'll love this role: The scientific challenge here is scale and signal: large-scale ML on enormous, high-velocity data, optimization and auction dynamics, and causal measurement of what actually moves the business. Generative AI and LLMs are tools you reach for when they help, not the point of the work. The impact also reaches beyond Amazon: we donated the Dynamic Traffic Engine (DTE) to the IAB Tech Lab as an open-source framework that lets demand-side platforms signal which bid requests they value, so supply-side platforms send fewer wasteful ones and QPS waste drops across the whole programmatic supply chain. We are a highly motivated, collaborative team with an entrepreneurial spirit and a broad mandate to experiment and innovate. You will work alongside talented engineers, product managers, and scientists in a culture that rewards bias for action, innovation, and experimentation. What makes this role unique is the combination of scientific rigor with real-world impact at a scale very few systems reach. Your impact and career growth: Amazon Ads is investing heavily in AI and ML, creating room for scientists to innovate and make their mark. As an Applied Scientist, you will own the science for well-defined supply-optimization problems and take your work end to end, from framing the approach through experimentation and into production with measured business impact. You will partner closely with engineers to productionize your models and with product managers to tie your science to customer and advertiser outcomes. You will share your findings, begin to mentor teammates, and grow your influence on the team's technical direction over time. This is your opportunity to do high-rigor applied science in one of the fastest-growing businesses at Amazon. Learn more about Amazon Ads: https://advertising.amazon.com/ Key job responsibilities As an Applied Scientist in Amazon Ads, you will: - Conduct hands-on data analysis and build large-scale ML models and pipelines for supply optimization. - Take your models end to end, from proof of concept through experimentation, optimization, and deployment into production, working closely with software engineers to productionize them and with product managers and fellow scientists along the way. - Design and run A/B experiments and causal analysis to validate hypotheses, draw insights from petabyte-scale data, and measure real business impact. - Research and apply advanced ML, including generative AI and large language models, to demand prediction and traffic filtering. - Drive end-to-end optimization projects that tackle ambiguous problems at massive scale, developing scalable, efficient processes for model development, validation, and deployment that optimize traffic monetization while maintaining customer experience.
